name: Art & Famous Paintings (AI-written, not yet reviewed)
description: 63 questions on art, painters and famous paintings, from easy to hard (20 easy, 23 medium, 20 hard), written by Claude. Every question and answer needs checking by a person before anybody plays it.

source.name: Written by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) on 2026-10-05, from its own knowledge plus the pages each item cites: no API call. Each item's `source` names the page its fact was confirmed on, or "common knowledge" with a reason where the fact is universal. Fact-check pending: no item carries `checked` yet, so a separate fact-check pass still has to go through every item, and a person still reviews it by playing.

review.how: Check every question, answer and explanation. Fix or delete what is wrong, set status to 'reviewed' with your name and the date, then move the file to packs/ and list it in pack_library.js.

items.question: Who painted The Starry Night?
items.explain: Van Gogh painted his swirling night sky in 1889.

items.question: Which artist painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
items.explain: Michelangelo painted the ceiling between 1508 and 1512.

items.question: What is Michelangelo's famous statue of David carved from?
items.explain: David was carved from a single block of white Carrara marble.

items.question: Who painted The Scream?
items.explain: The Norwegian painter Edvard Munch made The Scream in 1893.

items.question: In which famous museum does the Mona Lisa hang?
items.explain: The Mona Lisa has hung at the Louvre in Paris for over two hundred years.

items.question: If you mix blue paint and yellow paint, what color do you get?
items.explain: Blue and yellow mix together to make green.

source.note: Basic colour mixing taught to nearly everyone in school.

items.question: Vincent van Gogh painted a famous series of which flower?
items.explain: Van Gogh's bright yellow Sunflowers are among the best-loved paintings in the world.

items.question: Claude Monet painted many pictures of which flowers floating on his garden pond?
items.explain: Monet painted about 250 pictures of the water lilies in his garden.

items.question: What is the stand that holds an artist's canvas called?
items.explain: An easel holds the canvas upright while the artist paints.

source.note: Everyday art vocabulary known to nearly every adult.

items.question: What is the flat board an artist mixes paints on called?
items.explain: A palette is the board, often with a thumb hole, where painters mix their colors.

source.note: Everyday art vocabulary known to nearly every adult.

items.question: Andy Warhol famously painted cans of which brand of soup?
items.explain: Warhol's 32 Campbell's Soup Cans paintings are a famous piece of Pop Art.

items.question: Which country was the artist Pablo Picasso from?
items.explain: Picasso was born in Malaga, Spain, though he lived most of his adult life in France.

items.question: In the painting American Gothic, what is the farmer holding?
items.explain: The stern farmer in American Gothic holds a pitchfork.

items.question: What do we call a painting of a person?
items.explain: A portrait shows a particular person, often their face.

source.note: Basic art vocabulary known to nearly every adult.

items.question: Norman Rockwell painted hundreds of covers for which magazine?
items.explain: Rockwell painted 322 Saturday Evening Post covers over 47 years.

items.question: Who painted The Last Supper?
items.explain: Leonardo painted The Last Supper on a wall in Milan in the 1490s.

items.question: The painter Frida Kahlo came from which country?
items.explain: Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter famous for her self-portraits.

items.question: Which mountain can be seen behind the giant wave in The Great Wave print?
items.explain: Hokusai's Great Wave shows Mount Fuji small and snowy in the distance.

items.question: In Rodin's statue The Thinker, the man rests his chin on his what?
items.explain: The Thinker sits deep in thought with his chin resting on his hand.

items.question: Monet's painting Impression, Sunrise gave its name to which art movement?
items.explain: A critic borrowed Monet's title to name the Impressionists in 1874.

items.question: Who painted Girl with a Pearl Earring?
items.explain: The Dutch painter Johannes Vermeer painted it around 1665.

items.question: Which artist painted the melting clocks in The Persistence of Memory?
items.explain: Salvador Dali painted his soft, melting watches in 1931.

items.question: Who painted The Night Watch?
items.explain: Rembrandt finished his huge group portrait of Amsterdam's civic guard in 1642.

items.question: Who painted The Birth of Venus, with the goddess standing on a giant shell?
items.explain: Botticelli painted The Birth of Venus in Florence in the 1480s.

items.question: Who painted Nighthawks, the famous late-night diner scene?
items.explain: Edward Hopper painted Nighthawks in 1942.

items.question: Gustav Klimt's painting The Kiss shimmers because he used what?
items.explain: Klimt painted The Kiss in oil with real gold leaf.

items.question: Seurat built his painting of La Grande Jatte from thousands of tiny dots. What is that technique called?
items.explain: In pointillism, small dots of color blend together in the viewer's eye.

items.question: Jackson Pollock laid his canvases on the floor and did what?
answers: Rolled paint on with his feet
items.explain: Pollock's drip paintings made him a leading Abstract Expressionist.

items.question: What is painting onto wet lime plaster, as on the Sistine Chapel ceiling, called?
items.explain: In fresco, the paint bonds with damp plaster as it dries.

items.question: Who sculpted The Thinker?
items.explain: The French sculptor Auguste Rodin created The Thinker in bronze.

items.question: Georgia O'Keeffe, known for her giant flowers, also painted desert landscapes in which state?
items.explain: O'Keeffe lived and painted at Ghost Ranch and Abiquiu in New Mexico.

items.question: Who painted American Gothic?
items.explain: Grant Wood painted American Gothic in 1930, using his sister and his dentist as models.

items.question: Roy Lichtenstein's Pop Art paintings copy the style of what?
items.explain: Lichtenstein painted big comic-book scenes, dots and all.

items.question: Michelangelo's statue of David stands in a museum in which Italian city?
items.explain: David has stood in Florence's Galleria dell'Accademia since 1873.

items.question: Piet Mondrian painted black grid lines filled in with which three colors?
items.explain: Mondrian kept to the three primary colors plus black, white and gray.

items.question: Which brother, an art dealer, supported Vincent van Gogh throughout his career?
items.explain: Theo van Gogh gave Vincent money, encouragement and art-world contacts.

items.question: The Statue of Liberty's outer skin is made of which metal, which has turned green over time?
items.explain: Thin copper sheets weathered into the green patina we see today.

items.question: On a painter's traditional color wheel, which color sits opposite red?
items.explain: Red and green are complementary colors, so they sit across from each other.

items.question: American painter Mary Cassatt exhibited in Paris with which group of artists?
items.explain: Cassatt, a friend of Degas, showed her work with the Impressionists.

items.question: At about what age did Grandma Moses begin painting in earnest?
items.explain: Grandma Moses started painting seriously at 78 and kept going past 100.

items.question: Picasso's Blue Period was followed by which warmer period of pinks and oranges?
items.explain: Picasso's Rose Period, full of circus performers, ran from 1904 to 1906.

items.question: Monet's famous water-lily garden was at his home in which French village?
items.explain: Monet painted his flower garden and lily pond at Giverny for over 30 years.

items.question: The Lascaux cave paintings of horses and other animals are in which country?
items.explain: Lascaux is in the Dordogne region of southwestern France.

items.question: Who painted Las Meninas, with the young princess Margaret Theresa at its center?
items.explain: Velazquez painted Las Meninas in 1656; it hangs in the Prado in Madrid.

items.question: Who painted the triptych The Garden of Earthly Delights?
items.explain: Bosch's crowded, dreamlike triptych has been in the Prado since 1939.

items.question: Who painted the Arnolfini Portrait of 1434, with its round mirror and small dog?
items.explain: Jan van Eyck's oil-on-oak masterpiece hangs in the National Gallery, London.

items.question: Who painted The Hay Wain, a cart crossing the River Stour?
items.explain: Constable painted The Hay Wain in 1821, and it won a gold medal in Paris.

items.question: Who painted The Fighting Temeraire, an old warship towed up the Thames by a steam tug?
items.explain: Turner's sunset painting was voted Britain's favorite in a 2005 BBC poll.

items.question: Which two philosophers stand at the center of Raphael's The School of Athens?
items.explain: Plato points upward while Aristotle gestures out toward the world.

items.question: Who painted the 1851 picture Washington Crossing the Delaware?
items.explain: German-American Emanuel Leutze painted it in Dusseldorf; one version hangs at the Met.

items.question: Which museum is home to Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring?
items.explain: The painting has belonged to the Mauritshuis since 1902.

items.question: Which Italian word, meaning roughly 'smoked', names Leonardo's soft blending of tones without hard outlines?
items.explain: Leonardo blended colors 'in the manner of smoke', as in the Mona Lisa.

items.question: Which Baroque painter is famous for tenebrism, figures lit by a sharp shaft of light against deep darkness?
items.explain: Caravaggio pushed light-and-dark contrast to dramatic extremes.

items.question: What do painters call paint laid on so thickly that the brushstrokes stand up from the surface?
items.explain: Van Gogh and Rembrandt both used thick impasto paint.

items.question: In egg tempera paint, which part of the egg is usually mixed with the pigment?
answers: The whole egg beaten with oil
items.explain: Egg yolk thinned with water was the main paint binder before oil took over.

items.question: The precious blue pigment ultramarine was made by grinding which stone?
items.explain: Ground lapis lazuli made a blue that was at times as costly as gold.

items.question: The name 'Fauves', given to Matisse and Derain's group, means what in French?
items.explain: A critic called them 'wild beasts' for their bold colors at the 1905 Salon d'Automne.

items.question: Wassily Kandinsky formed which artists' group with Franz Marc and others?
items.explain: Kandinsky's group, Der Blaue Reiter, means The Blue Rider.

items.question: Which sculpture is the only work Michelangelo ever signed?
items.explain: He carved his name on the sash across Mary's chest in the Pieta in St. Peter's Basilica.

items.question: The Winged Victory of Samothrace in the Louvre shows which Greek goddess?
items.explain: Nike, goddess of victory, alights on the prow of a ship at the top of the Louvre's Daru staircase.

items.question: Leonardo da Vinci's Lady with an Ermine hangs in a museum in which city?
items.explain: It is on display at the Czartoryski Museum in Krakow, Poland.

items.question: Which Baroque sculptor designed the great curved colonnades of St. Peter's Square in Rome?
items.explain: Bernini built the two sweeping colonnades between 1656 and 1667.

items.question: Hokusai's The Great Wave belongs to which series of woodblock prints?
answers: One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
items.explain: The Great Wave is part of Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.
